claims.text: The starting material is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix.
CaF2 particles will be uniformly dispersed in the CoCrFeNi matrix through powder metallurgy or similar composite processing.
Embedded CaF2 particles will act as discrete lubricious sites.
Deformation and heating during sliding will cause the CaF2-containing sites to coalesce into a continuous interfacial tribofilm.
The CaF2-containing tribofilm will form in situ during sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
At lower temperatures, CaF2 particles will reduce interfacial shear resistance.
CaF2 is thermally stable and lubricious at elevated temperatures relevant to the proposed test range.
At elevated temperatures, CaF2 will mitigate direct metal-to-metal contact.
At elevated temperatures, CaF2 will mitigate oxidation at the sliding interface.
The CaF2-mediated mechanisms will preserve low friction and low wear across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The CaF2-dispersed composite will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the designated temperature range.
The CaF2-dispersed composite will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the designated temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction as temperature rises.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits variation in wear as temperature rises.
The proposed effect applies to ambient-atmosphere sliding at fixed normal load and sliding speed between approximately 25 and 800 °C.
